correctness.rationale: Established hypergeometric rooted-PD mean formula (Nipperess and Matsen 2012/2013) plus elementary triangular binomial inversion identifies precisely the length-weighted descendant-clade-size vector. Strict positivity turns its nontrivial support into the set of internal proper clade sizes. A complete unordered rooted full-binary recursive census produces all 1,1,2,3,6 shapes with two to six leaves and no repeated nontrivial supports. The explicit seven-tip height-marked trees have positive integer edges and height four, unequal 4-tip subtree shapes, identical spectrum (12,3,2,1,0,0), and exact two-tip distributions (1,4,4,12)/21 and (2,2,5,12)/21, variances 128/147 and 142/147. Equal-spectrum root grafting preserves the collision at each greater tip count. A standard-library rational checker was executed on the actual standalone script, independently enumerating all k-tip samples. Finite testing proves only finite base cases; graft induction proves every n at least seven.

evidence: Fischer, Hamann and Wicke (2025), Section 3.1 and Appendix A Fig. 11, reports first collision of the full clade-size multiset at nine tips and explicitly tabulates its multiplicities.
The present n=7 trees have different multiplicity-retaining clade-size sequences, but exactly matching sums of positive edge lengths within each clade size.
Chao et al. (2015) studies phylogenetic rarefaction and extrapolation; its target is expected diversity estimation, not unlabeled topology identifiability from full curves.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Identical full clade-size multisets is a stronger combinatorial condition than identical supports, while equal length-weighted clade-size sums is a metric condition neither implied by nor required to imply equal multisets. The 2025 first nine-tip multiset collision does not imply the present first seven-tip weighted-curve collision, nor does this result claim a collision of multisets at seven. The general rarefaction papers cover the mean formula but not sharp topological recovery.

evidence: Prior edge-presence formula implies full mean curves depend on weighted descendant-clade sizes, but it does not identify the first point where positive ultrametric trees can share those values.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: To derive the precise claim from existing formulae, one must additionally prove injectivity of nontrivial-size supports for every binary topology up to six tips; construct exact nonisomorphic clocklike trees with matching length-weighted spectra at seven; distinguish their full two-tip laws; and show an all-size graft continuation. These steps are not consequences of merely knowing the expected-PD expression or the nine-tip sequence collision without substantive new argument.

originality.rationale: Full open preprint of Nipperess and Matsen (2012), Sections 4–8, and 2015 open chapter of Nipperess credit and establish mean and variance formulas; their targets are expected/variance computation, not sharp topology recoverability. Chao et al. (2015) treats rarefaction/extrapolation, not first topology collision. Most importantly Fischer, Hamann and Wicke (2025), Section 3.1 and Appendix A Fig. 11, report the first duplicate *clade-size multiset* at nine tips, while the seven-tip examples here deliberately have different multisets and exactly matching *positive length sums by clade size*. Searches for tree-shape support, weighted clades, equivalences, minimal counterexamples, and complete curve identifiability did not reveal stronger direct coverage. An unindexed stronger result remains a bounded literature risk; lack of hits alone is not called proof of novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed general theorem on moment-equivalent ultrametric phylogenies or weighted clade-size support may already cover the seven-tip cutoff and its proof.
The published 2025 clade-size-sequence paper has a different invariant; do not mistake its n=9 threshold as corroboration of the n=7 result or as proof of uniqueness.
Scope is restricted to complete exact species-based rooted-PD mean curves with positive full binary trees; stronger or altered observation schemes may give different thresholds.

value.rationale: A complete expected species-based rooted-PD rarefaction curve is an ecologically interpretable object, and recovering tree shape from all its sampling levels is a natural identifiability question. The result gives a sharp finite cutoff and an actual positive-length ultrametric biological-model counterexample with different observable two-tip PD laws, quantifying what averaging loses rather than merely inventing an invariant. The exact full support classification through six and explicit all-size grafting give a reproducible boundary of use. It does not overclaim applicability to empirical noisy data or new methods for reconstructing general phylogenies.
